title: Trump Administration Aims to Clamp Down on A.I. Chip Loophole
summary: Also, new data paves the way for weight-loss drugs for children. Here’s the latest at the end of Monday.

The Trump administration announced today that it was advancing a rule[intended to make it more difficult for China](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/16/us/politics/trump-china-ai-chip-loophole.html) to use advanced A.I. chips made by American companies like Nvidia.


The rule would close what many in Washington see as a loophole: Despite a ban, China had been able to remotely access the advanced chips by renting them from data centers in Southeast Asia and elsewhere. The rule would require data centers to perform strict checks on their customers to determine if they are linked to a list of countries that includes China, Russia and Iran.


The plan arrived just before President Trump left on a trip to Asia, where he will travel to the Philippines[and then to China for an economic summit](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/15/us/politics/nvidia-trump-huang-china-xi.html) . In China, Trump is scheduled to meet with Xi Jinping, China’s leader, and President Vladimir Putin of Russia.


The debate has set Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who oversees chip policy, at odds with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, and tensions have spilled out into the open. Both Bessent and Lutnick are traveling with Trump on the Asia trip.


**For more:**


-


Trump said that he was open to seeing[Jensen Huang reinstated at Nvidia](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/16/us/politics/trump-jensen-huang-nvidia.html) .


-


A study found that the largest data centers in the U.S. are[responsible for as much carbon emissions as Denmark or Bolivia](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2026/11/16/climate/ai-data-center-pollution-carbon-emissions.html) and use more electricity than New York City and Los Angeles combined.
